newsitem.title: UK: UK Treasury's Jack says pound kept costs subdued.
newsitem.headline: UK Treasury's Jack says pound kept costs subdued.

text.p: British Treasury financial secretary Michael Jack said Tuesday's survey from the Confederation of British Industry showed a favourable outlook for orders and output while sterling's performance was keeping cost pressures down.
"I'm glad that today's CBI survey confirms the continued trend of rising business confidence," Jack said in a statement read by a Treasury official.
"It also shows a favourable outlook for orders, output and investment and it is clear that sterling's recent strength has helped keep cost pressures very subdued."
The CBI in its latest quarterly industrial trends survey said demand for British manufactured exports has levelled off for the first time since October 1993.
Manufacturing output grew steadily over the past four months although more slowly than expected. The CBI said a decision on whether interest rates needed to rise was finely balanced.
Twenty-three percent of firms reported higher export orders over the past four months and 24 percent reported lower orders, a negative balance of one percent.
A CBI official said the impact of sterling's strength was beginning to feed through to manufacturers' export orders.
